questions.questionText: The production possibility curve shows the maximum potential output of apples and pears for an economy using current resources. Y X apples W Z O pears Which pair of positions identifies an efficient and an inefficient outcome?

options.A: W and Y B W and X C X and Z D Y and Z

questions.questionText: The price of a good rises by 5% and the quantity of it demanded rises by 3%. At the same time, the incomes of consumers of the good rise by 4%. The law of demand appears not to be working in this case. What is the most likely explanation?

options.A: Other things did not remain equal.
options.B: The demand for the good was price inelastic.
options.C: The real price of the good fell.
options.D: The time period was the very short run.

questions.questionText: When is division of labour likely to be most effective?

options.A: in a large market with stable demand
options.B: in a market where consumers prefer a handmade product over a product made using machines
options.C: in a market where consumers require a variety of goods
options.D: in a small market where consumers require a custom-made product

questions.questionText: What will influence the value of the price elasticity of supply of a good?

options.A: the level of producer surplus
options.B: the time period under consideration
options.C: the total income spent on the good
options.D: whether the good is a necessity

questions.questionText: The quantity demanded of a product is given by Q = 400 – 10P, when P is the price in dollars. D Supply of the product is fixed at 100 units. If the price is $20, what will be the position in the market?

options.A: It will be in disequilibrium with excess demand of 100 units.
options.B: It will be in disequilibrium with excess supply of 100 units.
options.C: It will be in equilibrium with 100 units traded.
options.D: It will be in equilibrium with 200 units traded.

questions.questionText: A decrease in the quantity demanded of a product results in a proportionate decrease in sales revenues. What is true about its price elasticity of demand?

options.A: It is between zero and one.
options.B: It is infinite.
options.C: It is unitary.
options.D: It is zero.

options.A: an indirect tax

options.C: direct provision
options.D: provision of information

questions.questionText: The table shows the Gini coefficient for income in three countries. 2018 2019 2020 Costa Rica 0.479 0.478 0.497 New Zealand 0.330 0.326 0.320 Sweden 0.275 0.280 0.278 What can be concluded from this data?

options.A: All three countries have seen an overall improvement in income equality.
options.B: Costa Rica has the highest level of consumer income of all three countries.
options.C: New Zealand's income inequality worsened between 2018 and 2020.
options.D: Sweden's economy has the highest income equality of all three countries.

questions.questionText: Governments may have price stability as a macroeconomic objective. What is meant by price stability?

options.A: All equilibrium prices are maintained in the long run.
options.B: Demand-pull inflation cancels out any cost-push inflation.
options.C: Only disinflation is present in the economy in the long run.
options.D: Prolonged periods of inflation and deflation are avoided.

questions.questionText: A government decides to use supply-side policy to increase long-run aggregate supply (LRAS). What is the most likely reason why this policy tool will not lead to a fall in the price level?

options.A: Aggregate demand will also increase.
options.B: Labour productivity levels will increase.
options.C: Workers will save any extra wages they earn.
options.D: Workers will spend any extra wages on imports.

questions.questionText: What defines a progressive tax?

options.A: All taxpayers pay the same proportion of income in taxes.
options.B: Low-income earners pay a lower proportion of income in taxes than high-income earners.
options.C: Low-income earners pay less in taxes than high-income earners.
options.D: Low-income earners pay more in taxes than high-income earners.

questions.questionText: Country X trades with country Y. What are the terms of trade for country X?

options.A: average price of country X’s exports divided by the average price of country Y’s exports
options.B: the ratio of an index of country X’s export prices to an index of its import prices
options.C: value of country X’s exports divided by the value of country Y’s exports
options.D: value of country X’s imports divided by the value of country Y’s imports

options.C: When its interest rate exceeds that of its trading partners.
options.D: When its unemployment rate exceeds that of its trading partners.
